sources.title: Pamaree Surakiat, Territorial Expansion of the First Toungoo Empire in the mid-16th Century (2006)
sources.note: Direct journal abstract; issue 2(1), 2006. Article-platform 2013 citation timestamp is not the issue date. Distinguishes fragmented Irrawaddy basin from expanding Toungoo imperial system.

sources.title: Victor Lieberman, Ethnic Hatred and Universal Benevolence (2021)
sources.note: Full publisher PDF read, especially printed pp. 321 to 323. Reign dates follow this scholarly article, rather than discrepant dates in the state-news palace account.

sources.title: Myanmar Department of Archaeology and National Museum, King Bayinnaung Bell inscription nomination
sources.note: Direct UNESCO nomination PDF pp. 2 to 3, 5 to 7. Original trilingual bronze bell at Shwezigon, donated 23 May 1557. Royal conquest claims are political self-presentation. No unverified world-first or abolition claims repeated.

sources.title: Kanbawzathadi Royal Palace in Bago, Myanmar Digital News, 25 April 2020
sources.note: Direct official report, sections Archaeological excavations and Reconstruction of replica royal palace. Used only for excavation/reconstruction, not disputed reign chronology.

sources.title: Elizabeth Howard Moore, Exploring the East-West Cultural Corridor: Historic and Modern Archaeology of Bago and Dawei (2014)
sources.note: Kyoto University CSEAS newsletter, direct text. Bago paragraphs and aerial/satellite figure caption. Do not repeat the article’s problematic 1548 Ayutthaya conquest date.

sources.title: U Thaw Kaung, Bayinnaung in the Hanthawadi Shinbyumya Shin Ayedawbon chronicle
sources.note: Indexed original PDF printed p. 8, weights and port commodities. Conservatively grouped with chapter 4 of the same collection already used by the Shan card; combined work budget checked separately.

sources.title: Toru Ohno, The Administrative Institution and the Social Structure of Burma during the Nyaungyan Dynasty (1985)
sources.note: Direct scholarly English abstract; palace layout and records transmission from edicts of Nandabayin, Nyaungyan, Anaukpetlun and Thalun. Article discusses a wider 17th/early-18th-century period; copy keeps attribution to the study.

sources.title: Andrew Huxley, Lord Kyaw Thu’s Precedent: a Sixteenth-Century Burmese Law Report (2012)
sources.note: Original scholarly chapter indexed text, printed pp. 229 to 230 and 246. Direct PDF returns 403. Reproducible searches: site:burmalibrary.org "Huxley" "Shin kyaw thu pyatton"; "Kyaw Thu" "1870" "manuscript" Huxley; site:burmalibrary.org "Kyaw Thu" "eldest son". Title is verified scholarly Roman transliteration; no invented Burmese script.

sources.title: Ralph Fitch’s journey, in Robert Kerr, A General History and Collection of Voyages and Travels, volume 7 (1824)
sources.note: Direct full text, Chapter IX section II, paragraphs beginning From the bar of Negrais; In your house, however; He sits in judgment; In Pegu, there are many priests; They go about. Fitch departed Bengal for Pegu on 28 November 1586. Kerr warns of borrowing from Cesar Frederick, so observations are attributed to the published account rather than treated as independent corroboration or population-wide measurements.

batchIdentityNotes.note: One exact indexed record only. No alias to pegu, ava, bagan, pagan-1279 or burma. Decoded northern outline changes at 1530, never approximates Bayinnaung’s maximum empire and leaves Pegu separately mapped. Public overview states this. Period breaks organize historical phases inside imported 1492 to 1650 bounds, not exact uncontested accession dates. Prior Konbaung card for burma is preserved.
